A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scaling-law study. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model simulations, Sobolev-task MLP and vision CNN experiments, and C4 transformer and linear-network experiments in Appendices A and G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation and neural-network results in the main text and appendices, alongside additional CIFAR-5M kernel diagnostics.

M1.justification: The two-layer model, fixed initial feature projection, projected SGD updates, squared-error objective, and gamma-controlled feature evolution remain unchanged in Equations 3–4. Added architecture descriptions document existing experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic power-law regression, Sobolev functions on the circle, MNIST-1M, CIFAR-5M, and C4 language modeling. The transformer experiment in v2 Figure 9 already appeared in v1 Figure 8; the new CIFAR diagnostics retain existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same lazy or linearized-network comparisons, feature-learning settings, and theoretical reference curves. The new CIFAR diagnostic varies widths and training checkpoints without introducing a competing method.

E3.justification: New Figure 8 adds a diagnostic evaluation across CNN widths N=8–256 and training checkpoints through t=4×10^6, reporting eigenspectra and cumulative task-power curves. Existing loss-evaluation protocols are retained; newly stated architecture details do not establish changed training settings.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 8 adds CIFAR-5M analysis of kernel spectra across widths and task alignment during training, examining the spectral assumptions and feature-learning mechanism. Existing SGD-noise, easy-task, and linear-network spike analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains means and shaded error bars over 32 random experiments. No run counts, seeds, or uncertainty-estimation procedures change; the added finite-size-fluctuation footnote explains existing error bars.

E6.justification: New Figure 8 reports spectra supporting alpha approximately 2 and the previously stated CIFAR source exponent beta approximately 0.075, plus increasing task variance captured by the leading eigenmode. Matched loss curves and Table 1 entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2.1 adds approximate gamma-dependent transition-time and loss-prefactor derivations, also reflected in Equation 11. Equation 6 removes the inconsistent lambda_k^(-beta) relation. The original DMFT, bottleneck, and compute-optimal derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions retain the same claims: a solvable feature-learning model, improved exponents for hard tasks, compute-optimal scaling predictions, and nonlinear-network support. The added introduction summary restates the optimization-trajectory interpretation.

C2.justification: New Appendix H distinguishes NTK evolution from useful task-aligned feature learning and explains that neither alone guarantees improved scaling. Section 4 adds an interpretation involving instability of the kernel approximation outside the RKHS. Existing CIFAR-5M limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the MLP depth of 4, width of 512, forward-pass parameterization, and input sampling. Appendix A also specifies MNIST's two convolutional and two dense layers and identifies the CIFAR residual architecture. These are disclosures about retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds comparisons with Chizat, Kunin, and Tu et al. (2024). Appendix B.1 explains the relationship to earlier random-feature DMFT analyses, while Appendix H adds representation and kernel-alignment references. The central research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. v2 organizes Appendix A into task-specific subsections, adds B.1, E.2.1, and H, shortens the main DMFT overview, and makes localized explanatory and conference-header edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel CIFAR diagnostic in Figure 8, relocates several existing figures and Table 1, and renumbers later figures. Figures 5–6 receive limited caption additions; existing plots and the overall document design remain.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Appendix A provides useful architecture details and CIFAR spectral evidence, while Appendix H clarifies what feature learning means and what it does not guarantee. These improve reproducibility and interpretation without changing the main empirical conclusions. The new E.2.1 summary has a local sign inconsistency between item 3 and Equation 72, but this limited defect does not outweigh the gains.
